summary: Results-review pass for the sim10 bulk-target sweep (512 KiB / 4 MiB / 8 MiB, batch 100, one BD/GPU/CUDA stream) at f171fdb16. Every claim in README.md and validation.json that I could check against the copied native evidence under build/bulk-review-evidence matched exactly: six full cases each delivered 10,000 events and 33,582,000,000 payload bytes; completed reader requests were 50,000 / 9,454 / 4,599 per target with requests==completed_requests and requested==completed bytes; every read-size histogram in the native rank-2 io blocks is identical to the frozen expected-reference.json (and to the offline frozen-B planner check); callbacks per run were 100 / 4,356 / 2,233 with identical subbatch histograms across both repeats, each summing to 10,000 events; the callback stream pointer is a single value per case (grep count equals callback count); cpu_reads=0 and pressure_drains=0 in all cases; the rank-2 drain block is closed/pending 0/active 0/held 0/peers 1; initial_cache shows 0 resident pages for all five payload files in every case (preflights included) and final residency computes to 0.99997487; host sdfampere042, GPU GPU-1b50deab…/0000:01:00.0, CuPy 14.0.1, KvikIO 26.10.00, compat ON, 8 threads/1 MiB task/16 MiB bounce/auto-direct OFF, framework {batch 100, streams 1, budget 6 GiB, smd 1000}, 56 shared physical cores and NUMA interleave are identical across all six cases; source_sha256 and runtime_files hashes are identical across cases and provenance.json; stage directory was removed (cleanup.json) and the job finished COMPLETED 0:0 in 5m50s with an empty .err. The derived numbers in README (mean read sizes, 2.154/1.574/1.719 GiB/s means, 26.9% and 20.2% deltas, 320.26/17.61/38.43 MiB peaks, NIC RX GiB per run, 0.93–1.03 MiB/s idle RX) all recompute from the native values. SBT-02 is resolved: README explicitly couples read size, small-group ownership (peak pending 500→5) and execution-cut effects (100 callbacks of 100 → thousands of 1–5/1–11), states no section timings exist, and says it does not show larger reads alone are slower or that storage bandwidth is the limit. Two new low, non-blocking wording items: SBT-04 asks the README to define 'peak outstanding/pending reads' as submitted-but-not-yet-retired via wait_batch (not proof of 500 concurrent storage I/Os), which the coordinator already plans; SBT-05 notes the NIC bracket for case 04 was 4.3 s wider than the timed loop versus ~0.9–1.2 s elsewhere, so 'slightly wider' should give the range. SBT-01/SBT-03 remain deferred cleanup. Nit (not a finding): README line 75 reads as if the preflight order list includes six entries; reword to separate preflight order from full-run order. I could not execute audit.py, test_audit.py, or any hash; those results are taken from tests.log and the coordinator's statement.

findings.evidence: README lines 5-9 present callbacks/run, events per subbatch and peak outstanding reads beside reader calls and GiB/s; lines 19-27 state that the small-group restriction allows one live small group per file, that 100 callbacks of 100 became thousands of 1-5/1-11 event callbacks, that no section timings were collected, and that this 'does not show that larger reads alone are slower, or that storage bandwidth is the limit'; lines 34-39 give the full subbatch histograms, which match the native callbacks (grep counts 100/4356/2233 and histogram sums of 10,000 events).
findings.requested_change: Resolved. No change required; keep this coupled wording intact when adding the SBT-04 counter definition.

findings.evidence: README table header 'Peak outstanding reads' and line 20-21 'Peak pending reads fell from 500 to 5' plus line 24 'reduced input concurrency' are not defined. bulk_accounting.py lines 18-26 count a request as outstanding from KvikioGpuReader._submit_read until wait_batch retires its future; 500 is exactly 100 events x 5 files submitted before the batch wait. KvikIO serves these with 8 worker threads and 1 MiB tasks, so the counter is a submission-window peak and some reads may already have completed physically; it does not prove 500 concurrent storage I/Os.
findings.requested_change: Add one sentence defining the counter: 'peak outstanding/pending = requests submitted to the GPU reader and not yet retired via wait_batch; physical I/O for some may already have finished, so this is not evidence that 500 reads were simultaneously active at storage.' Soften 'reduced input concurrency' to 'reduced the number of reads submitted ahead of the wait' or similar. Coordinator already plans this; evidence-only edit.

findings.evidence: README says NIC totals include 'a slightly wider timing bracket'. Native nic_delta.seconds vs timed seconds: case 00 15.26 vs 14.29, 01 21.24 vs 20.02, 02 18.40 vs 17.50, 03 19.82 vs 18.95, 05 15.62 vs 14.75, but case 04 (04-target-4194304.json lines 46489/46500) 24.05 vs 19.72, i.e. 4.3 s (22%) wider. At the measured idle rate (~1 MiB/s) this adds only a few MiB to the 33.4 GiB total, so the reported bytes are not materially affected, but 'slightly' understates case 04.
findings.requested_change: State the bracket excess range explicitly (about 0.9-1.2 s for five runs, 4.3 s for run 04) or add a 'NIC bracket s' column to the per-run table, and note that per-run NIC RX totals are not rates and were not used for GiB/s.
